about: The moth's close-range details (docs/moth-9, Bean's ask of Nov 25: 'hone in on detailed elements and make sure to model them well'): the parts a camera a metre away sees, drawn from what the class's boats carry in general (no maker's part copied: shapes from the photos in refs.json and from the class rules, sizes typical). Metres. Each part names the object it joins: an object that already exists takes the extra geometry (so it moves with that part in the game), a new one is made with its slot.

wand_fitting.note: the wand's bow fitting: a compact head round the pivot at the end of the carbon bowsprit, the axle's ends standing out of it, the ride-height knob on top of it (it sets the wand's angle against the pushrod), a base plate where the bowsprit meets the deck, a short lever above the pivot that drives the pushrod aft along the deck, the shock cord from a horn on the head's nose that holds the wand forward, and the ferrule of the two-piece wand. Round 1 had two loose cheeks and the knob standing on the bowsprit; close-range reviewers read them as plumbing

strut_head.note: where the main strut leaves the deck: its flange (the case's top), the bellcrank's housing on top of the strut, and the gearing adjuster: a slotted arm aft of the housing with a knob that slides along it (more or less flap for a degree of wand)

rudder_head.note: the gantry's end: an alloy block that takes the four tubes, upper and lower gudgeons round the rudder's pin, the rudder's own stock above them that the tiller clamps to, and a saddle under each tube's foot on the deck and the transom

elevator_pod.note: the junction's bulb where the elevator pivots on the rudder's foot

rig.note: the mast's step plate, the gooseneck clamp, the spreader brackets and their tip caps, the hounds tang, the masthead's cap, the wires' swaged ends, a saddle and an adjustable tang on each wing bar where a shroud lands, and the forestay's deck tang, each with its shackle

blocks.note: every block is drawn as one: two cheeks, the sheave between them, the axle's caps and the shackle on top; the ratchet is the largest, on a base plate

lacing.note: the mesh's lacing: a line wrapped round the frame's tube (over, down the outside, under) and back to the mesh's edge every 4 cm, all round each wing

wing_sockets.note: the brackets on the hull's deck edge that the wings' front and rear bars plug into

grip.note: the twist grip's ribs and its rubber end cap

joint.note: the tiller's universal joint: a moulded rubber joint between the tiller and the extension

luff_sleeve.note: the sail's luff sleeve: the mast's section grown 14% with a 12 mm tail aft where the cloth leaves it, from the tack to the head (close-range reviewers saw a gap between the sail and the mast)

boom.note: the gooseneck's toggle and pin, the boom's end cap and the clew's car under it

sail_note: The sail's other details (batten pockets, head and clew boards, corner patches, stitching) are the game's sail material (M_SailCloth's Detail, boat fidelity 4), drawn from the sail's UVs on the live cloth, so none are geometry here.
